lens: Owner and access-sensitive user; first encounter; simulated AI panel seat
reason: The public proposition is clear, and the supplied desktop/mobile hero captures show coherent Precision Instrument hierarchy and readable actions. I traced Home → Join → Apply materials/review in source, plus owner People → account setup → incident queue → resolution. Applicant copy accurately distinguishes the stripped written packet from the identifying original resume. New-account failures preserve uncertain state, use opaque operational references, and restrict lookup identity to current cycle owners. Resolution explicitly records remediation rather than claiming account repair. However, the existing-account recovery branch lacks equivalent partial-failure handling. Supplied SQL, Node and synthetic browser evidence support bounded local claims, not observed owner recovery or broad world-class acceptance. No hosted integration or human success evidence exists.

findings.evidence: ADD_EXISTING_USER calls ensure_external_identity, returns a generic 409 on identity error, and then grants membership without the incident handling used by ADD_USER. A returned grant error falls through to generic handling at lines 288-291; a transport exception escapes this branch. The initiating useRushAction shows only “Request failed” on transport failure (src/app/admin/rush-controls.tsx:81-83). ensure_external_identity can activate a profile and claim allowlisted memberships before this later grant (20260905120000_membership_allowlist.sql, ensure_external_identity).
findings.userImpact: An owner using the existing-account path to recover preserved provisioning can encounter another partial or uncertain write without a durable recovery reference or guidance to inspect current access. The incident queue can therefore omit an unresolved recovery attempt; a generic failure does not explain what may already have changed.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply opaque incident recording and explicit reconciliation guidance to uncertain identity and failed/uncertain grant outcomes for existing accounts, preserving all access. Add focused tests for committed-but-unacknowledged identity/grant writes and incident-storage failure on this branch.
